sphere-volume-solid.name: Volume of a sphere
sphere-volume-solid.oneLiner: The formula that finds the volume of a sphere by multiplying the cube of the radius by pi and four thirds
sphere-volume-solid.description: The volume of a sphere is the radius multiplied by itself three times, then multiplied by pi and by four thirds. Use it to find how much space a perfectly round object such as a basketball takes up.

V.description: The amount of space the sphere takes up.

\\frac{4}{3}.description: The fixed coefficient that sets the volume of a sphere.

\\pi.description: The circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, about 3.14159.

r.description: The distance from the centre of the sphere to its surface.

r^3.description: The radius multiplied by itself three times. Volume is three-dimensional, so the radius is cubed.

realWorldExamples: Working out the volume of a basketball
Estimating the volume of the Earth
Comparing the sizes of marbles

sphere-surface.name: Surface area of a sphere
sphere-surface.oneLiner: The formula that finds the surface area of a sphere by multiplying the square of the radius by pi and four
sphere-surface.description: The surface area of a sphere is the square of the radius multiplied by pi and by four. It is exactly four times the area of a circle with the same radius. The surface area is precisely the area you would need to cover if you painted a ball.

S.description: The area of the entire surface of the sphere.

4.description: It says that the surface of a sphere is four times the area of a circle of the same radius.

\\pi.description: The circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, about 3.14159.

r.description: The distance from the centre of the sphere to its surface.

r^2.description: The radius multiplied by itself twice.

realWorldExamples: The total area of leather on a football
How much paper you need to cover the surface of a globe

cylinder-volume.name: Volume of a cylinder
cylinder-volume.oneLiner: The formula that finds the volume of a cylinder by multiplying the area of the circular base by the height
cylinder-volume.description: The volume of a cylinder is the area of its base (the area of a circle) multiplied by its height. Think of it as a round base stacked upwards to the full height.

V.description: The amount of space the cylinder takes up.

\\pi.description: The circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, about 3.14159.

r.description: The radius of the circular base of the cylinder.

r^2.description: The radius multiplied by itself twice. It sets the area of the base.

h.description: The distance between the top and bottom faces of the cylinder.

realWorldExamples: Working out how much a drinks can holds
The capacity of a cylindrical water tank

cylinder-surface.name: Surface area of a cylinder
cylinder-surface.oneLiner: The formula that finds the surface area of a cylinder by adding the two bases and the curved side
cylinder-surface.description: The surface area of a cylinder is the area of the two circles at the top and bottom plus the area of the curved side. Unroll the side and you get a rectangle whose width is the circumference of the circle and whose height is the height of the cylinder.

S.description: The area of the entire surface of the cylinder.

2.description: The coefficient factored out as a common term.

\\pi.description: The circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, about 3.14159.

r.description: The radius of the circular base of the cylinder.

h.description: The distance between the top and bottom faces of the cylinder.

realWorldExamples: Working out the area of the label on a drinks can
How much wrapping paper it takes to cover a cylindrical gift box

cone-volume.name: Volume of a cone
cone-volume.oneLiner: The formula that finds the volume of a cone by multiplying the area of the circular base by the height and dividing by 3
cone-volume.description: The volume of a cone is the area of its base multiplied by its height and divided by 3. It is exactly one third of a cylinder with the same base and height.

V.description: The amount of space the cone takes up.

\\frac{1}{3}.description: It says that a cone has one third the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height.

\\pi.description: The circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, about 3.14159.

r.description: The radius of the circular base of the cone.

h.description: The perpendicular distance from the apex of the cone to its base.

realWorldExamples: Working out how much an ice cream cone holds
The volume of a party hat

cone-surface.name: Surface area of a cone
cone-surface.oneLiner: The formula that finds the surface area of a cone by adding the circular base and the curved side
cone-surface.description: The surface area of a cone is the area of its circular base plus the area of its curved side. Unroll the side and you get a circular sector whose area is the radius times the slant height times pi.

S.description: The area of the entire surface of the cone.

\\pi.description: The circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, about 3.14159.

r.description: The radius of the circular base of the cone.

l.description: The slanted distance from the apex of the cone to the edge of its base.

realWorldExamples: The area of paper needed for a party hat
Working out the fabric area of a conical tent

cuboid-volume.name: Volume of a cuboid
cuboid-volume.oneLiner: The formula that finds the volume of a cuboid by multiplying length, width, and height together
cuboid-volume.description: The volume of a cuboid is length times width times height. It is the same as multiplying the area of the rectangular base by the height, and it amounts to counting how many unit cubes fit inside the box.

V.description: The amount of space the cuboid takes up.

realWorldExamples: Working out the volume of a delivery box
How much water fits in a swimming pool
Estimating the interior capacity of a refrigerator

cuboid-surface.name: Surface area of a cuboid
cuboid-surface.oneLiner: The formula that finds the surface area of a cuboid by adding the areas of three faces and doubling
cuboid-surface.description: The surface area of a cuboid is the sum of the areas of its three distinct faces, multiplied by 2. A cuboid has three pairs of opposite faces, and the faces in a pair have the same area, so you add the three kinds of face and double the result.

S.description: The area of the entire surface of the cuboid.

2.description: You multiply by 2 because the opposite faces come in three pairs.

lw.description: The area of the face given by length times width.

lh.description: The area of the face given by length times height.

wh.description: The area of the face given by width times height.

realWorldExamples: How much wrapping paper it takes to cover a gift box
Working out the outer surface area of a delivery box

tetrahedron-volume.name: Volume of a regular tetrahedron
tetrahedron-volume.oneLiner: The formula that finds the volume of a regular tetrahedron by multiplying the cube of an edge by the square root of 2 over 12
tetrahedron-volume.description: The volume of a regular tetrahedron is the cube of one edge length multiplied by the square root of 2 divided by 12. A regular tetrahedron is a solid whose four faces are all identical equilateral triangles, the simplest of the regular polyhedra.

V.description: The amount of space the regular tetrahedron takes up.

\\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{12}.description: The fixed coefficient that comes out of the geometry of a regular tetrahedron.

a.description: The length of one edge of the regular tetrahedron. Every edge is the same.

a^3.description: The edge length multiplied by itself three times.

realWorldExamples: The volume of a pyramid-shaped chocolate
Working out the size of a tetrahedral die (D4)

pyramid-volume.name: Volume of a pyramid
pyramid-volume.oneLiner: The formula that finds the volume of a pyramid by multiplying the area of the base by the height and dividing by 3
pyramid-volume.description: The volume of a pyramid is the area of its base multiplied by its height and divided by 3. It is exactly one third of a prism with the same base and height. Use it for solids with a polygonal base and a pointed top, like the Egyptian pyramids.

V.description: The amount of space the pyramid takes up.

\\frac{1}{3}.description: It says that a pyramid has one third the volume of a prism with the same base and height.

B.description: The area of the polygonal base of the pyramid.

h.description: The perpendicular distance from the apex of the pyramid to its base.

realWorldExamples: Estimating the volume of an Egyptian pyramid
Working out the interior space of a pyramid-shaped tent
